newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian death on trail to Heartbreak Hotel.
newsitem.headline: Australian death on trail to Heartbreak Hotel.

text.p: A dirt track in outback Australia leads to the remote Heartbreak Hotel, but for two men the road led to death this week when their truck broke down in hellish temperatures of almost 50 degrees Celsius (122 Fahrenheit).

The two men, both Aborigines, broke cardinal rules of travelling in the outback, where only a thin line separates life and death -- they told no one where they were going, ran out of fuel and water and tried to walk for help.
One man, aged 20, was found dead on the roof of the twin-cab utility truck and his 42-year-old companion was found about 20 km (12 miles) away, severely dehydrated and in shock.

The Heartbreak Hotel is in one of the most remote and harshest parts of Australia's Northern Territory called Cape Crawford -- a few billion years ago it used to be the coast, but today it is searing desert.
The nearest "civilisation" is the town of Borroloola, two and a half hours drive away with your foot flat to the floor.
Darwin, the capital of the Northern Territory, is 730 km (453 miles) northwest as the crow flies -- by road its a few hundred extra kilometres (miles).
"This is heartbreak Australia out here. Many things can break your heart from the heat to the loneliness," Susie McManis, manager of the Heartbreak Hotel, told Reuters by telephone on Wednesday.
McManis said the savannah country has been hot lately with temperatures ranging around 50-55 Celsius (122-131 Fahrenheit) and 46 Celsius (114 Fahrenheit) under the shade of a tree.
On Saturday the two aboriginal men left Limmen Bight River for Borroloola, but their truck ran out of diesel on the Roper Bar dirt road, a Borroloola police officer told Reuters.
The men spent the night in their truck. Come sunrise as the temperature began to rise a passing motorist said he would return with fuel for their truck.
Late on Sunday, after receiving the fuel, the truck again broke down, suffering mechanical difficulties only 30 km (18 miles) from the Heartbreak Hotel.
In the sweltering conditions one man decided to walk to the hotel, but never made it.
Twenty-four hours after running out of fuel he was found collapsed on the side of the dirt track suffering severe dehydration -- he was only 10 km (six miles) from the Heartbreak Hotel.
His companion was found dead on the roof of the truck.
"People here always tell someone where they're going...and we give them three hours extra and then start searching," said McManis. "They broke the rules."
